title: The real cost and quality of AI generated assets
author: Global-Error9905
selftext:
Want to hear how people use generated assets in their games.

I used AI model web to test how far I could go with free credits and evaluate how usable the results would be. So far, it actually looks promising. Before I pay for it, I want to figure out how much it costs, so I can pay based on my time and money.

While I work on my multiplayer RPS game and I want assets to have a consistent style. Instead of using lots of different assets, I am trying to create a repeatable framework in my prompts:

1\* Put a set of standardized prompt templates for different types of assets, I will then need to repeatedly promt and modify framework until I get consistency in the generation of assets.

2\* Generate 3-view reference images.

3\* Use these images in AI model web to generate a 3D model. Once complete, split the model into parts and export STL.

4\* Import STL into Blender to reduce poly count, do some cleanup, and apply textures.

5\* Import assets into Unity for testing and rigging.

Has anyone actually used generated assets on a larger scale project? How much did this cost you and how much work did you need to do yourself?

I am still looking into alternatives and methods for asset generation, so if this takes a long time and costs a lot of money I will be looking for business who do custom asset.

comments.body:
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4275290/The\_Cold\_Cases\_Remembering\_Jory/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4275290/The_Cold_Cases_Remembering_Jory/)

  
I did all the game design, writing, and most of the code myself, but I had to use ai for the pictures because i wanted real looking photos and i don't know anyone who looks like the people I want to use, plus I can't afford to hire actors and models and shooting locations :P

comments.author: ModernGameDev
comments.body: I make 2D games so it’s a bit easier to generate the assets as references and bring it over to affinity or asesprite and trace over it so I have a true asset (vector or pixel) to have more control over animations and stuff

comments.author: Kindly-Sail6260
comments.body:
Since we’re using AI, I decide to use AI for the AI. 

Using the estimate above: **about $10–$15 per finished, game-ready asset total.**  
So **1,000 assets ≈ $10,000–$15,000 total**, including AI generation + estimated human cleanup/integration labor.

That’s pretty much it. It’ll more than likely be the same with business everywhere unless you want something dirt cheap but that’s quality at that point. Hope that helps
